title: Basis Figure Where an Appraisal Report Stands on the Piece
content:
# Service Training Note: The Basis Figure Where an Appraisal Report Stands on a Piece

## The rule the desk applies

Where a piece at the bench of the Belrose Workshop Repair and Resizing Service has an appraisal report standing on it under the Belrose Appraisal and Gemological Services, the basis figure the carried value is built on is taken from that report rather than from the counter.

1. Where an appraisal report stands on the piece and is still current at the handling date, the basis figure is the value that report states.
2. Where an appraisal report stands on the piece and has run out, the basis figure is the greater of the value that report states and the value the piece was taken in at.
3. In any other case the basis figure is not taken from a report.

## Questions answered

**When is a report still current?** When the last day the report is treated as current has not passed at the handling date. A report whose last current day falls on the handling date itself is still current.

**What if the report states less than the counter figure and has run out?** Clause 2 takes the greater of the two, so the value the piece was taken in at stands as the basis figure.

**What if the report states less than the counter figure and is still current?** Clause 1 takes the value the report states, whether it is the greater of the two or not.

**Hypothetical readings.** A piece taken in at 5,000.00 USD with a current report stating 8,000.00 USD has a basis figure of 8,000.00 USD; with a current report stating 4,000.00 USD, a basis figure of 4,000.00 USD. The same piece with a report that has run out stating 8,000.00 USD has a basis figure of 8,000.00 USD, and with a report that has run out stating 4,000.00 USD, a basis figure of 5,000.00 USD.
